transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-11-02
- Start: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Redwood Prod), Janelle Reyes (Tellara Head of ML), Mark Dwyer (Tellara Infra), Priya Nair (Tellara PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, this is Maya from Redwood, AE for your account. Quick round robin?
[00:08] Janelle: Hey I'm Janelle, head of ML at Tellara, leading the NLU squad, excited to see the catalog fit today.
[00:14] Mark: Mark here, infra, I'll be focused on constraints and what we can host inside our VPC.
[00:20] Priya: Priya, product, curious about cost profiles and rollout implications.
[00:26] Ethan: Hi all, Ethan SE — I'll walk through the compatibility matrix and bench integration.
[00:32] Maya: Great. Agenda: shortlist criteria, bench integration to your CI, kernel/hardware compatibility, routing policies, and security. Any quick asks?
[00:45] Janelle: We have two app classes — real-time chat NLU (latency 120ms p95 target) and batch analytics. We'll need different model picks.
[00:55] Ethan: Perfect, we'll show how the catalog surfaces model latency buckets and quantization options, and how Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quant profiles.

[02:10] Ethan: Jumping into the console — first tile is the catalog. Here we filter for open-source models with good GLUE-like bench scores and small-medium context memory. Note there's a "compatibility" column which maps to kernel families and GPU types — we visible show cuda-11 kernels, Triton-ready, and quantized int8-optimized variants.
[02:45] Janelle: Quick question — how often are bench numbers refreshed? We need something that maps to our payloads.
[02:52] Ethan: Bench numbers are curated but you'll want to run our microbench; the catalog shows reference metrics (50k token distribution) and then we add a customer-specific bench layer you can drop into CI.

[04:12] Maya: For the shortlist criteria, we usually recommend starting with a 3-model shortlist: one high-accuracy float baseline, one quantized mid-cost model, and one lightweight low-latency variant for p95-sensitive endpoints.
[04:28] Priya: That matches our product goal. How do we reason about accuracy delta when moving to int8? We've seen hallucination rate changes.
[04:36] Ethan: Good point. Redwood Optimize includes a quality monitor and regressions alert tied to a prompt set. In practice, it's often an acceptable delta for NLU intent classification if your prompts are covered; for generative tasks you might keep float for high-fidelity lanes. Also you can pin model versions and route slower requests to higher-fidelity variants.

[06:05] Mark: On the infra side, our primary cluster is A100-ish but for cost we want to test some T4/RTX variants with int8. How does kernel selection work?
[06:14] Ethan: The runtime inspects the model and picks kernel paths based on architecture and sequence length. In the compatibility matrix we mark which kernels are available per hardware. For example, some 4-bit kernels run best on Hopper/Blackwell family, other int8 kernels are optimized for Ampere—there's a mapping column in the matrix. Note: some kernel names in the UI are abbreviated (we sometimes show 'kv-cash' instead of 'KV cache' in the auto transcripts, sorry for the UI quirk).

[07:40] Janelle: Can we attach our own benchmark suite? We want reproducible numbers in our CI.
[07:45] Ethan: Yes — you can upload your prompt set into the bench UI or link a Google sheet. Redwood will run customer microbench with your input distribution and produce a CSV you can pull into your CI. We'll also surface cost/token estimates and a latency distribution breakdown.

[09:10] Maya: Security — Tell us your blocker list: VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log retention requirements?
[09:18] Mark: We require KMS for key management, private deployment or at least a VPC endpoint for the control plane, and audit logs kept 12 months.
[09:26] Maya: Good, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and an optional on-prem control plane. I will send the SOC2 summary and our private-deploy checklist after the call.

[11:05] Priya: How do you handle rollouts across variants? We don't want a noisy canary to suddenly increase cost.
[11:14] Ethan: We support canary rollouts with a percent traffic split and automatic fallback policies. If latency or error rate breaches SLO, traffic fails over to the fallback model variant. You can also set cost thresholds so a spike in token usage can trigger an autoscale cap.

[13:00] Janelle: About metrics — does the console show token-level cost? We want to tie experiments to product KPIs.
[13:08] Sofia: Yes, the Console has token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards. You can break down by prompt templates, model variant, and then see cost per 1k requests, etc. We also export JSON for invoices or internal reporting.

[15:22] Ethan: Now the compatibility matrix walk: here's a sample row for the "OpenLM-14B" variant — shows memory footprint, recommended kernel (fused-attn-v2), compatibility with 40GB/80GB GPUs, and which quant profiles are validated.
[15:37] Mark: If we pick a quant profile validated on Ampere but run on T4, do numbers translate?
[15:44] Ethan: They won't be identical. That's why we recommend running the microbench on your target hardware. The matrix shows validated combos but adding your CI bench is the only way to get exact p95 numbers.

[17:40] Janelle: A practical ask: can Redwood produce a CSV that maps prompt templates to recommended model variant for us to import into our routing layer?
[17:49] Maya: Yes — we can generate a picklist export that maps route names, safety tags, and recommended variants with a confidence score. That export integrates with routing rules in the Console.

[20:10] Ethan: I'll demo a small bench run — this is simulated: request payloads, 1000 samples, measuring p50/p95, tokens per response, and cost estimate. Watch the p95 climb on the float variant vs int8 at different batch sizes.
[20:40] Janelle: Seeing those numbers helps. For chat NLU we need to preserve p95 under 120ms — is that feasible with the hybrid approach (int8 plus a float fallback)?
[20:50] Ethan: Typically yes. You can route primary traffic to the int8 variant and route long-tail or failed cases to float. Also prefix KV cache helps for repeated conversational context.

[23:05] Mark: On the network front, if we do Private deployment, what's the control plane egress? We want minimal outbound.
[23:12] Maya: With Private you can opt for a local control plane and reduce egress — we have an air-gapped option for stricter regimes. We'll add the network diagram in the follow-up pack.

[25:30] Priya: Pricing — how do we estimate monthly cost for a pilot?
[25:36] Maya: We'll provide a ballpark: per-token hosted pricing vs dedicated reserved capacity. For pilots we often recommend short reserved pool for predictable throughput; Redwood Optimize also suggests batch sizes to reduce net cost. I'll include a sample calc in the email.

[28:00] Ethan: A note about kernel mismatch — sometimes a model will run but with suboptimal kernel choices leading to higher latency. The console flags those rows as "compat-warning" so you don't accidentally pick an unsupported combo.

[30:10] Priya: Any experience with hallucination regressions post-quant? We need examples.
[30:20] Ethan: We've seen small regressions in open gen models for long-form generation; for classification/regression tasks it's often negligible. Our quality monitoring can run A/B checks against a golden prompt set and alert if regression exceeds threshold.

[33:00] Janelle: Let's talk timeline — we want pilot in November and evaluate in December. Who needs to be involved?
[33:07] Maya: AE + SE for setup, your infra contact for VPC peering (Mark), and product for success criteria (Priya). We'll provision catalog slice and a shared bench sheet.

[35:30] Ethan: I'll note three technical next steps: 1) run the microbench on Tellara payloads, 2) produce compatibility CSV for routing, 3) push sample bench CSV to your CI pipeline.

[37:50] Mark: For the bench, we'll share a smaller dataset first — about 500 samples — to avoid quotas.
[37:58] Janelle: We'll also add edge-case prompts for intent collisions.

[40:10] Sofia: Sharing artifacts now: Maya will send deck (catalog-demo-deck.pdf) and Ethan will upload a bench-results template (bench-results.xlsx). Links: [redwood.link/catalog-demo-deck], [redwood.link/bench-template].

[42:30] Maya: Recap: Redwood to share security docs and pricing; SE to run customer microbench and provide CSV; Tellara to share prompt set and infra constraints.
[42:44] Priya: Sounds good. One more: can we schedule the deep bench sync for Nov 10?
[42:51] Maya: Yes, we'll propose times after the call.

[44:00] Janelle: Small nit — in the compatibility table, can we see an estimated cost impact per 1k requests per variant? That would help PM decisions.
[44:10] Ethan: The Console shows cost per 1k in the variant detail and the Optimize module can project monthly spend. We'll include that in the pilot sheet.

[47:05] Mark: If the pilot looks good, what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[47:12] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed throughput and predictable latency bands; I'll include the Dedicated plan summary in the follow-up.

[49:30] Priya: Thanks — quick thanks from our side, this was helpful.
[49:36] Maya: Appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the artifacts and confirm the Nov 10 deep bench sync.
[49:43] Janelle: Thanks everyone.
[49:46] Ethan: Bye all.

Meeting end.
